explanation: The holy place where God dwells and is worshiped, central to Ezekiel's vision of future Israel.
Ritual acts in which animals or food are offered to God as a form of worship and atonement for sin.
The religious leaders in Israel who performed sacrificial rites and served in the temple on behalf of the people.
One of the twelve tribes of Israel with special duties and responsibilities connected to the temple and its services.
The innermost part of the temple where God's presence was strongest, also called the Most Holy Place.
The process of dividing the land of Israel among the twelve tribes, described in detail in Ezekiel 45.
A leader or ruler in Israel, often referred to as a king or prince. In Ezekiel 45 this may refer to a messianic figure.
Religious celebrations and feasts in Israel, such as Passover and the Feast of Tabernacles, where the people gather to worship God and remember his deeds.
